_Ecency - Decentralized social, built for the Web3 generation._ * * * Already on Hive? Link Your Existing Account to MetaMask ======================================================= _Keep your history, gain a new way to sign in._ * * * If you've been on Hive for a while - whether through Ecency, PeakD, or any other Hive frontend - you already have an account with a set of cryptographic keys tied to it. You don't need to start over to use MetaMask. Ecency lets you add MetaMask as an additional signing method to your existing Hive account. Here's what that means and how to do it. * * * How It Works ------------ Hive accounts support multiple sets of keys. When you link MetaMask to your existing Hive account, Ecency generates a new set of keys associated with your MetaMask wallet and adds them alongside your existing keys. The result: **your account now has two ways to log in and sign transactions**: 1. Your original Hive keys (unchanged, still fully functional) 2. Your MetaMask wallet (new, added via this process) Nothing is removed or replaced. You can use either method going forward. * * * What You'll Need ---------------- * Your existing Hive account credentials (posting key, active key, or master password) * MetaMask installed and set up with at least one active wallet * * * Step-by-Step: Link MetaMask to Your Hive Account ------------------------------------------------ ### 1\. Log In to Ecency with Your Existing Account Go to [ecency.com](https://ecency.com) and log in using your current Hive keys or Keychain. * * * ### 2\. Go to Account Settings Navigate to your **Profile Wallets** or by **directly going** look for the [**Link Metamask**](https://ecency.com/wallet/setup-external) section. * * * ### 3\. Connect Your MetaMask Click **Link MetaMask**. Your browser will open the MetaMask prompt asking you to connect. Approve the connection. * * * ### 4\. Authorize the Key Addition Ecency will ask you to sign an authorization using your existing Hive keys to confirm that you own this account and are approving the addition of new keys. This is a one-time step to prove ownership. Once confirmed, the MetaMask-linked keys are added to your Hive account. * * * ### 5\. You're Done From this point forward, you can: * **Log in to Ecency with MetaMask** - no need to paste your Hive keys * **Sign all transactions with MetaMask** - posts, votes, transfers, and more * **View your multichain wallet** - your Ethereum, Solana, BNB, and other MetaMask-linked addresses now appear in your Ecency wallet page * **Still use your original keys** - nothing about your existing setup has changed * * * Why Link MetaMask? ------------------

Benefit

Details

Easier login

No more copying and pasting private keys

Multichain wallet view

See all your Web3 assets in one place

Familiar UX

Sign transactions the way you already do across Web3

No key replacement

Your original keys remain intact and usable

* * * A Word on Security ------------------ Linking MetaMask does not expose your existing private keys to MetaMask, and it does not give MetaMask control over your original keys. The new MetaMask-linked keys are separate - they are simply an additional authorized set for your account. As always, keep your MetaMask seed phrase and Hive master password safe and offline. * * * Welcome to the Full Ecency Experience ------------------------------------- Whether you're a longtime Hive user or just arrived via MetaMask, Ecency is built to give you full ownership of your content, your identity, and your assets - across multiple blockchains, from one platform. If you haven't explored your wallet page yet, now's a great time. You'll find all your connected chain balances, transfer options, and more - all signable with MetaMask. * * * _Need help? Reach out to the Ecency community on_ [_ecency.com_](https://ecency.com) _or find us on social media._ _Ecency - Your decentralized home on the blockchain, since 2016._

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23t6zEBxjcig8UoL2ehL4aovdmDLskx75zbmq8mQ388YZf1TnEEMaiCDynrivHyNgTAQU.png)





There are moments where you sit in front of your screen and genuinely ask yourself: why am I even doing this? Not because the work isn't enjoyable. Not because I don't know what I'm doing. But because you realize — once again — that the people you're going out of your way to help simply don't care. I'm not writing this out of anger. Well, maybe a little. But mostly I'm writing it because I feel the community deserves to know — how some projects in this ecosystem treat people who invest their personal time to protect their users.
#### Wenn Sicherheit zur Einbahnstraße wird — meine Erfahrung mit Responsible Disclosure im Hive-Ökosystem Es gibt Momente, da sitzt man vor dem Bildschirm und fragt sich ernsthaft: warum tue ich das eigentlich? Nicht weil die Arbeit keinen Spaß macht. Nicht weil ich nicht wüsste, was ich tue. Sondern weil man mal wieder feststellt, dass die Leute, für die man sich einsetzt, das schlicht nicht interessiert. Ich schreibe diesen Artikel nicht aus Wut. Na ja, vielleicht ein bisschen. Aber hauptsächlich schreibe ich ihn, weil ich das Gefühl habe, dass die Community das wissen sollte — wie manche Projekte in diesem Ökosystem mit Menschen umgehen, die ihre persönliche Zeit investieren, um deren Nutzer zu schützen.
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23t72XfWcbYhmHtjAezAoEdKGTaBSSVWWQW9WjgAXjeAb24D37jjFNzeVaQHMLhKuGA4T.png)
### The Context: What Security Research Actually Means Before I get into it, I want to clarify something that gets misunderstood constantly. Yes, there are AI tools. Yes, they help identify vulnerabilities faster, categorize them, and turn them into reports. That's great — and I use them too. But what happens between "AI found something" and "a finished, professional disclosure report is on the table" — that is anything but automatic. That is hours upon hours of personal work. It means building proof-of-concepts, recording videos, setting up webhook endpoints, switching NordVPN exit nodes, documenting, documenting again, calculating CVSS scores, assessing the real-world impact on actual users, writing remediation recommendations, and packaging all of it so a developer can act on it immediately. No AI tool sits down at night and records dual-browser proof-of-concept videos. That's the human. Me. With my time. For free. And that is exactly the point where appreciation — or the lack of it — makes all the difference.
### Der Kontext: Was Security Research wirklich bedeutet Bevor ich anfange, möchte ich eines klarstellen, weil es immer wieder missverstanden wird. Ja, es gibt KI-Tools. Ja, die helfen dabei, Schwachstellen schneller zu erkennen, zu kategorisieren und in Berichte zu verwandeln. Das ist großartig und ich nutze das auch. Aber was zwischen "KI hat etwas gefunden" und "fertiger, professioneller Disclosure-Report liegt auf dem Tisch" passiert — das ist alles andere als automatisch. Das ist Stunden um Stunden eigener Arbeit. Das bedeutet: Proof-of-Concept bauen, Videos aufnehmen, Webhook-Endpoints einrichten, NordVPN-Exit-Nodes wechseln, dokumentieren, nochmals dokumentieren, CVSS-Scores berechnen, Auswirkungen für echte Nutzer bewerten, Remediation-Vorschläge ausarbeiten und das alles so aufbereiten, dass ein Entwickler es sofort umsetzen kann. Kein KI-Tool setzt sich nachts hin und zeichnet dual-browser Proof-of-Concept Videos auf. Das macht der Mensch. Ich. Mit meiner Zeit. Kostenlos. Und genau das ist der Punkt, an dem die Wertschätzung — oder das Fehlen davon — den Unterschied macht.
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23tGRC6hQD3WUqwoxrAFJmpyikxgAJhHVz2rkAHM3gT1kxyyrsEgpD2MmG7mFqrJdAzWT.png)
### What I Found — Without Giving Too Much Away I discovered a security vulnerability in a well-known Hive platform. A vulnerability that affects every single user who visits a specific publicly accessible page — no login required, no interaction needed, just opening the URL. I won't publish the technical details here yet, because the vulnerability has not been fixed at the time of writing. Responsible disclosure means giving the company a fair chance to resolve the issue before it goes public. That's the standard. I'm sticking to it — even though it's testing my patience at this point. What I can say: I didn't just take a screenshot and fire off an email. I delivered a complete audit report — with CVSS score, CWE classification, OWASP categorization, proof-of-concept videos, webhook logs containing real third-party user data captured involuntarily, remediation recommendations, and a full disclosure timeline. This was not a "hey I think something might be off" email. This was professional work.
### Was ich gefunden habe — ohne zu viel zu verraten Ich habe eine Sicherheitslücke in einer bekannten Hive-Plattform entdeckt. Eine Schwachstelle, die jeden einzelnen Nutzer betrifft, der eine bestimmte öffentlich zugängliche Seite besucht — komplett ohne Login, ohne Interaktion, einfach durch das Öffnen der URL. Ich werde die technischen Details hier noch nicht veröffentlichen, weil die Lücke zum Zeitpunkt dieses Artikels noch nicht gefixt ist. Responsible Disclosure bedeutet, dass man dem Unternehmen eine faire Chance gibt, das Problem zu beheben, bevor man es öffentlich macht. Das ist der Standard. Den halte ich ein — auch wenn er mich inzwischen an den Rand meiner Geduld bringt. Was ich sagen kann: Ich habe nicht nur einen Screenshot gemacht und eine E-Mail geschrieben. Ich habe einen vollständigen Audit-Report geliefert — mit CVSS-Score, CWE-Klassifizierung, OWASP-Kategorisierung, Proof-of-Concept Videos, Webhook-Logs mit realen Drittnutzer-Daten die unfreiwillig betroffen waren, Remediation-Vorschlägen und einer vollständigen Disclosure-Timeline. Das ist kein "hey ich glaube da ist was komisch"-E-Mail. Das ist professionelle Arbeit.
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23t74p8U5MCv45mFU6mbXbFJWLD92DWXMuEiBEpFBczXB5Hr8fQ9QYkXKGTQdtVwhp2Ey.png)
### The Response: A Masterclass in Indifference I submitted the report and waited for a reaction. What I received was — and I say this without exaggeration — one of the most remarkable emails I have ever gotten in this context. The core of the message, paraphrased freely: *We receive a lot of security reports that cost us a lot of time. We can't afford this. Also, you don't play the game anymore and you've sold your assets — so we can't be sure your motivations are really in the best interest of the game. Please don't send us anything further.* **I had to read that twice.** The suggestion that my motivations are questionable because I no longer hold in-game assets is like a hospital telling a doctor: "You're not sick yourself, so why should we trust your diagnosis?" Security is not a matter of personal stake. Security research is a matter of expertise, responsibility, and — yes — basic respect for the people who use a platform and trust that someone is keeping watch. All of this, as I later found out, was personally approved by the CEO. Good to know.
### Die Antwort: Ein Meisterwerk der Gleichgültigkeit Ich habe den Report eingereicht und auf eine Reaktion gewartet. Was ich bekommen habe, war — und ich sage das ohne Übertreibung — eine der bemerkenswertesten E-Mails, die ich in diesem Kontext je erhalten habe. Der Kern der Nachricht, frei zusammengefasst: *Wir haben sehr viele Security-Reports, die uns viel Zeit kosten. Wir können uns das nicht leisten. Außerdem spielst du das Spiel ja gar nicht mehr und hast keine Assets — also wissen wir nicht ob deine Motivation wirklich im Interesse des Spiels liegt. Bitte schick uns nichts mehr.* **Ich musste das zweimal lesen.** Die Aussage, dass meine Motivation fragwürdig ist, weil ich keine Ingame-Assets mehr besitze, ist so als würde ein Krankenhaus einem Arzt sagen: "Du bist selbst nicht krank, also warum sollten wir deiner Diagnose vertrauen?" Sicherheit ist keine Frage persönlicher Betroffenheit. Sicherheitsforschung ist eine Frage von Fachwissen, Verantwortungsgefühl und — ja — dem Respekt gegenüber Menschen, die eine Plattform nutzen und darauf vertrauen dass jemand aufpasst. Das alles wurde, wie ich später erfuhr, vom CEO persönlich abgesegnet. Gut zu wissen.
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23tRp515pPYob8whvg3PuS4xh3sSV4Tmfvfq5RiKZ6Sw4Xbus5BsEp7z9keUXgfch6Loa.png)
### Bug Bounties: Between Goodwill and Being Brushed Off I want to talk briefly about bug bounties here, because the topic is still treated as an afterthought in the crypto and Web3 space. A bug bounty program is not a gesture of generosity. It is a safety net — for the company. It creates a structured, fair channel for external researchers and ensures that vulnerabilities get reported before they get exploited. Companies like Google, Microsoft, or major DeFi protocols pay five figures for critical findings — not because they have to, but because they've understood that it's cheaper than the damage afterwards. What I've received so far for my work: a one-time payment of $10. As a “gesture of goodwill.” For another report I had submitted a few days earlier. A few years ago, things were even better, and I was treated much better. I'm not saying I want to get rich doing security research. But ten dollars for hours of documented work is not appreciation — it's a statement about how much security actually matters to that company.
### Bug Bounties: Zwischen Goodwill und Abspeiseung Ich möchte an dieser Stelle kurz über Bug Bounties sprechen, weil das Thema im Crypto- und Web3-Bereich noch immer stiefmütterlich behandelt wird. Ein Bug Bounty Programm ist keine Geste der Großzügigkeit. Es ist ein Sicherheitsnetz — für das Unternehmen. Es schafft einen strukturierten, fairen Kanal für externe Researcher und sorgt dafür, dass Schwachstellen gemeldet werden, bevor sie ausgenutzt werden. Unternehmen wie Google, Microsoft oder große DeFi-Protokolle zahlen im Fünfstelligen für kritische Lücken — nicht weil sie müssen, sondern weil sie verstanden haben, dass das günstiger ist als der Schaden danach. Was ich bisher für meine Arbeit bekommen habe: einmalig 10 Dollar. Als "Goodwill-Geste". Für einen anderen Report, die ich gemeldet hatte ein paar Tage zuvor. Vor einigen Jahren sah das noch besser aus und wurde viel besser behandelt. Ich sage nicht, dass ich reich werden will mit Security Research. Aber 10 Dollar für Stunden dokumentierter Arbeit ist keine Wertschätzung — das ist eine Aussage über den Stellenwert den Sicherheit in diesem Unternehmen hat.
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23swhwUNTE6qiswwBJfwVnNzR3YgSNFvHtBXJcM7DXiuK6CVnUwCsB8vpnroqmX1zitjF.png)
## What Happens Next I'm not going to sit on this indefinitely. That wouldn't be a responsible way to handle the knowledge. After the standard 90-day responsible disclosure window expires, I will publish everything — fully, technically, with all details. Until then: the company has everything it needs to fix the problem. What they choose to do with that is entirely up to them. **I've done my part.**
### Was jetzt passiert Ich werde die Lücke nicht für immer unter Verschluss halten. Das wäre kein verantwortungsvoller Umgang mit dem Wissen. Nach Ablauf der standardmäßigen 90-tägigen Responsible-Disclosure-Frist werde ich alles veröffentlichen — vollständig, technisch, mit allen Details. Bis dahin: das Unternehmen hat alles was es braucht, um das Problem zu beheben. Die Entscheidung was sie damit machen liegt bei ihnen. **Ich habe meinen Teil getan.**
--- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/louis88/23u5TAH2jC1DbsrZHy5UhFEEYfcSKm6ejRPonfAvUhYmbipUSH6fYyCTgQW3dxiav5wGR.png)
## Closing:
Why I'll Keep Doing This Anyway I won't stop reporting security vulnerabilities. Not because it always pays off. Not because I'm always treated with respect. But because at the end of the day, real people stand behind these platforms — people who had nothing to do with their CEO not wanting to read an email. But I will be very deliberate about where I invest my time going forward. And I will pay very close attention to how projects in this ecosystem treat the people who voluntarily help make it safer. **Because security is not a one-way street. And neither is respect.**
## Abschluss:
Warum ich das trotzdem weiter mache Ich werde nicht aufhören, Sicherheitslücken zu melden. Nicht weil es sich immer lohnt. Nicht weil ich immer respektvoll behandelt werde. Sondern weil am Ende echte Menschen hinter diesen Plattformen stehen, die nichts dafür können dass ihr CEO keine Lust hat, eine E-Mail zu lesen. Aber ich werde mir sehr genau überlegen, bei wem ich meine Zeit investiere. Und ich werde sehr genau hinschauen, wie Projekte in diesem Ökosystem mit Leuten umgehen, die freiwillig dazu beitragen es sicherer zu machen. **Denn Sicherheit ist keine Einbahnstraße. Und Respekt auch nicht.**

I like to cook if there's someone else to help eat the food, but it's a bit of a chore to really "cook" when oneself is the only one that will be eating it. Most of the time, I "fix" something simple instead of really "cooking" in the traditional sense. A common meal for me might be a piece of chicken tossed into the oven directly from the freezer — let it thaw and cook at the same time. Partway thru the cooking time, I might toss a prepackaged, single-serve cup of rice into the microwave and let it go for the recommended 3.5 minutes. Then, I might open a can of sliced beets or carrots to go along with it. Easy-peasy, yet still a balanced meal (entrée with protein, a starchy side, and a veggie) with minimal time in the kitchen since it's only myself to enjoy it.

When I do cook, I like it to feed me for at least two or three meals, if not more. One of my favorites in that vein is Meatloaf. I am not vegetarian or vegan, but this recipe can easily be adapted for those who are! So, please read on, even if you are an exclusively plant-based diner!

This dish was mentioned in a conversation with @mondoshawan a few months ago, but I never posted the recipe because I kept forgetting to take photos until I was eating already. Another more recent conversation with @solominer & @hurtlocker in the Hive Discord finally reminded me to do it again and take those "before, during, and after" shots. This particular recipe was also never written anywhere until that conversation with Solominer & Hurtlocker; it was slowly developed in my head from years of making it. I daresay, though, that it probably resembles meatloaf recipes from many other cooks, I haven't checked any lately. To be honest, it's very likely the synthesis of several recipes I may have read forty or fifty years ago, coupled with conversations with my mother, grandmother, aunts, and other women, and all distilled into one, tidy meatloafy cluster in my brain.

This recipe — as are most recipes! — is a general guide to making a dish. There is a lot of room for tweaks due to personal taste or proclivities. So, I will not give exact measurements for most of the ingredients; add salt & pepper to suit your taste, omit the cayenne pepper if you don't like the heat it brings, and so forth. Just "wing it" with me and go with whatever flow speaks to you!

For the vegans and vegetarians, substitute to your heart's content! When I say "meat," I'm referring to the main ingredient of the dish. For you, that could be tofu, tempeh, mushrooms, crumbled veggie burgers, lentils, etc. And when say "eggs," feel free to use chia seeds soaked in water that you might normally use instead of eggs. The results should be the same, or close to it.

Measured Ingredients

* one pound (454 grams) of ground meat *(beef, turkey, lamb, etc., or substitute)* * one package of Lipton® Recipe Secrets™ dry soup mix * two large eggs (or substitute)

Even with the "measured" ingredients, there's a lot of room for play. If you have a package of meat that is a little more, or a little less, than one pound, it's not a problem. With a half-pound of meat (225 grams), maybe only use one egg. Or if you have a big family to feed, use 1.5 or 2 pounds of meat and add another egg or two, whatever looks right.

The use of Lipton® Recipe Secrets™ dry soup mix is something I learned from my mother as a child. She always made hamburger patties with that soup mix added, and it makes them sooooo good! I always think of her when I use it. There are different flavors of their product available nowadays: Onion, Onion Mushroom, Beefy Onion, Vegetable, etc., and any of them will be fine. OR... if you don't have (or don't want to use) that item, you can use your own seasonings. You could also use bouillon — even a vegetable bouillon! — if you prefer. Knorr® makes a fabulous vegetable bouillon that I use sometimes in other dishes. If you live in Africa, consider Maggi®, instead. There are similar products in other parts of the world, too, just check your local market.

I usually make my meatloaf in a Pyrex™ glass baking dish, the size of a 9"x5" (23cm x 15cm) loaf pan. The above photo shows the meat with the Lipton® Recipe Secrets™ dry soup mix sprinkled on top, before adding the other ingredients. I do all the mixing in the dish which I use for baking, thus saving on the kitchen cleanup afterwards! 😁

Unmeasured Ingredients

* bread crumbs * onion * mushrooms, carrots or other veggies (optional) * salt, pepper, thyme, cayenne pepper (all optional and "to taste")

The bread crumbs are to provide "body" to the dish. Use any kind you like, seasoned or not. I use plain, since I have my own seasoning palette. You can buy bread crumbs already prepared at your market, or you can make your own by toasting bread (this is an excellent use for old bread that you're about to throw out anyway) and crush it into crumbs. If you make your own bread crumbs, any type of bread will suffice!

The eggs are simply there to help the dish hold together without its being crumbly in texture. I would not recommend adding less than the equivalent of 2 large eggs for a pound of meat/substitute, but more than two is fine. You can always use more bread crumbs if the mixed ingredients seem too liquid to hold together. So, if you have eggs that are medium or jumbo size, just use however many "feels" right to you.

One ingredient that I forgot to photograph in the first shot is onion! I hope everyone knows what an onion looks like. I love onions, especially the "sweet" variety, which is almost always what I buy for most of my cooking. Any size onion is fine, and you can use as much, or as little as you like. I often add an entire onion in my meatloaf! Plus, I usually add some onion powder, too. 😋 You can dice the onion into large or small pieces, your choice. I have an electric chopper which I dearly love. A short pulse or two will leave the food in small pieces, but a long, sustained press of the switch will mince small, or even purée, the onion. Any cut is fine, as we're adding it for the flavor more than anything. Below is my chopper, one shot of the blades (left), the other the whole appliance (right, with the electrical cord hidden behind the unit).

At this point, you can add other ingredients that you might like. Chopped carrots, chopped mushrooms, chopped celery, chopped peppers (bell, jalapeño, poblano, whatever kind you might like). Use your imagination, or just leave the veggies out if you wanna be a "purist" about the meatloaf. I'm usually a purist, and serve the veggies on the side. HINT: If your kids don't wanna eat their veggies, sneak some in here, for their health's sake. 😉

I stir everything together with a spoon. Back in grandma's day, cooks just used their hands, but I think that's kinda gross. That is how I learned, though, by using my hands to mix the ingredients; it's how my mother taught me and her mother before her. I don't think it's as sanitary, both for the food's sake as well as one's own personal hygiene. If some of that ground meat gets under fingernails and not thoroughly removed afterwards, the cook is spreading germs to everything s/he touches. So, I have used a spoon to mix, for many, many years.

And, for gosh sakes, if you do use your hands, please wash them afterwards, thoroughly, with hot, soapy water! Raw meat — especially ground meat — has bacteria that can cause illness, or even be fatal, if consumed before cooking. Even some of the famous chefs on television make me cringe when they handle raw meat and then grab the handle of their skillet, their stirring spoon, then wipe their hands on a towel before draping it over their shoulder. Germ city! ☹️

Once all the ingredients have been thoroughly mixed, I usually level the top of the meatloaf with the back of a spoon. Then, I squirt ketchup all over it. This is optional, and the amount of ketchup used is totally the cook's choice. When I buy ketchup, I always look for brands that have none of that High Fructose Corn Syrup crap in them. There is no sense in adding mega-doses of needless sugar into food. 😖

If you're not a fan of ketchup, don't use any. Or maybe just a drizzle or two. Or totally cover the meatloaf like I do! LOL! In lieu of ketchup, slices of fresh tomato would be good on top, or a can of diced tomatoes if you make it before the fresh ones come into the garden! Salsa would also be good on top, or a nice pico de gallo, or slices of peppers that would roast nicely as the meatloaf cooks. Or use barbecue sauce instead of ketchup. Or leave it naked. Yes, naked in the kitchen can be a fun thing sometimes. 😂

Now your masterpiece is ready to go into the oven. Hopefully, you turned your oven "ON" as you began prepping the dish so it is fully pre-heated. If not, remember to do that next time. Any temperature between 350°F and 400°F is good. I usually go with 375°F. For those in the metric world, set your oven between 180°C and 200°C, I'd go with 190°C right in the middle. Then bake it for one hour. After removing from oven, of course, let it "rest" on the stovetop for a couple minutes before digging into it.

During the conversation about meatloaf in the Hive Discord, Solominer reminded me that he makes his meatloaf with a cottage cheese stuffing. When I saw his recipe last year, I meant to try it but keep forgetting. Be sure to peek at his Cottage Cheese Stuffed Meatloaf recipe and let him know if you try it!

And the following photo shows a nice hunk of meatloaf, all plated and ready for your choice of side dish(es), perhaps Creamed Spinach, Pickled Beets, or Glazed Carrots. Maybe a smattering of Garlic Mashed Potatoes? I'm drooling already!

And the beauty of my technique is: You don't have gobs of stuff to wash afterwards if you mix it in the baking dish like I do. I wash the knife which I cut the onion with, the blades & basket of the chopper, and the spoon I stirred it all with. No other bowls or utensils are messed up. Cleanup is easy-peasy! ✨

If you make this meatloaf, please come back and report any substitutions or tweaks you made to it so others may be inspired! That goes especially to you who are vegetarian or vegan!

昨天发帖说儿子参加理化实验考试的事情——就是走个形式，全员满分。不过英语听力口语考试大概就没那么好糊弄啦。


![9310a695-06b9-4245-8e2f-84d41b13e10c.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcWLFaZc8x4L8eCniztChFyG1Rb5in3unpM3J9KqL1Jx8/9310a695-06b9-4245-8e2f-84d41b13e10c.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)


因为和理化实验教师随意给分不同，英语的听力口语一部分是电脑自动判分，对就是对，错就是错，这可没法造假呢。

因为英语听力口语考试也是计入中考总分，学校对这个可是相当重视，不像理化实验完全是放任的状态，英语听力口语一直抓得很紧。

怎么抓的呢？那就是使用一款叫做英语E听说的软件，每周（包括寒暑假）都要留几套听力口语测试，一直坚持了快三年。

这个软件确实也很好用——当然了，不是免费使用的。我感觉儿子的听力口语都得到了很大的提高。

其实儿子小学时，他妈妈就带他听各种英语绘本，有时候也让他朗读，所以说起来，诸多科目中，英语的听力和口语还算是他的强项呢。





![Weixin Image_2026-04-09_171247_782.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQma4G2Z2tm6KA8yb4z3CHm7qr5X4u15UmJrqfpDi43SdqB/Weixin%20Image_2026-04-09_171247_782.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)





因为是强项，所以做E听说时就总是很敷衍，有时候人家那边还没读完他就各种答题，各种跳过，原本应该十几二十分钟弄完的事情，他三两分钟就搞定。

对此，虽然我们也告诫过他要好好答题，重视起来，但也没觉得有啥大问题，之所以快，还不是因为会嘛？

不过正是因为我们全体没重视这个事，昨天的英语听力模考就翻车了呢。

儿子回来给我讲述，口语环节回答问题时，都是在滴的一声后开始回答。但是平时他跳（skip）习惯了，又按着旧习惯想跳过去，但是考场不提供跳过去的选项，他一疏忽，没等滴声响起，就开始回答。

等到滴声想起来，他才发现自己搞错了，然后慌乱地重答，过程中，把会读的单词也读错了。他为此非常沮丧。

我倒是觉得通过模拟考试翻车发现问题是大大的好事呢，不然直接到考场上实战再发生这样的问题，可就是真的惨了呢！

现在发现，以后再做E听说的时候重视起来，规规矩矩地答题，不去毛毛躁躁地跳过，就可以轻轻松松地避免这样的问题。


![2655d2b3-27fe-4e51-b600-7134ed26c5e1.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTyY5mo5wyTi6iAX2CA5kTr8NrQYPqa4aRQWoDA6VeXGR/2655d2b3-27fe-4e51-b600-7134ed26c5e1.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

儿子听我这么说，总算不那么沮丧，开心了一点点呢。然后给我说考场上的趣事，比如有个同学被考试用的大耳麦把头夹迷糊了，考试后直接请假回家。

哈，竟然这么夸张，我说一定是这娃原本就身体不舒服吧？儿子说不是，是这个女孩头比较大，所以夹得比较紧。晕，他竟然这么说人家小女孩，若是被人听到，不得挠他呀，哈哈哈哈。

![zekely5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/23tvqBNLv25vQjtcXePKD6xuQffp4CsdUkyxAwB23qPh1axo2qF2V8u97epfdV2kWrUNK.jpg)
The last Weekly Zekely a month ago so I owe you a bit of winter ending adventure! I know sometimes fewer words and more images is preferred so I will keep it brief and fill in the desired details in comments.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# Last Time on Your Zekely
![IMG_8210 (1).JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/EoCh5xsjRdV9U6VVtHHHdkC6FsVHanpJdVMcgWjBnbqi8YDqztcQ5qThxAAaD3F52Xt.JPG)
A month ago, winter was still battling to stay in power. The sun was starting to offer a little warmth and there was still a white blanket over the dog park.
![IMG_8545.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ6TquAbne31m35pom1ZukWGDQmJPfR9Nmsrp8BoNxreL/IMG_8545.JPG)
It still is wintery enough for me at present with milder days with a few more minutes of sunlight each day. The snow is melting nicely now and temperatures forecasted to reach 17 Celsius / 63 Freedom Units may be the end of it all! It has rained a few days after this shot so the park is plenty swampy right now.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# Business
![IMG_8351.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmajzzedueLe2fYts2D4Ri49LtmN3AhXznKvLUss8Z3k6n/IMG_8351.JPG)
Last month seemed like a whirlwind with all the work-related stuff. Always plenty to build and do, then there are networking events piled on top of that. I try and kill 2 birds with one stone by attending business gatherings in order to get out on the town and hopefully build a business relationship or two.
![IMG_8316.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmagZVqe9AGduY3ReqcG5UUzwrP1w5tVsD9h2LG8wrEf96/IMG_8316.JPG)
This one was more of a community gathering than a business meeting but same motivation. Support the helpers and sacrifice some downtime for connection.
![IMG_8572.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYBqLTL7bG8d73FtMaeUF3aajCZM2etpxE3KPri8WSdjg/IMG_8572.JPG)
This is a neat one. I work with the downtown business association who decided to have a job fair for locals to connect with businesses. We counted 500 jobseekers through the doors and the employers were drinking from the firehose before the busy season.
![IMG_8520.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXsEvc3LHnQFcDFLL6x3KcPypPRTGLwVq6MrWqQHbrLV2/IMG_8520.JPG)
Before you think we are done, one more. This one is a chamber of commerce meeting at a beer shop I have mentioned a few times for #beersaturday It really doesn't get much better than gathering with other business owners, supporting a new establishment and enjoying some free beer in the process!
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# Did Someone Say Beer?
![IMG_8476.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc9wDmt7ngjdMR3wqFTQrcGHeDDJrymT41uYMo99Z6GU5/IMG_8476.JPG)
We had a few brew sessions of our own this month. Brewmaster is headed overseas for a couple weeks vacation so we brewed a couple extra batches so the fridges were full while he is sipping wine. This one is a NEIPA now in kegs and I should get to them in the next week or two.
![IMG_8541.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZhSnMchYzABBuVf997tokTmZBUWB4sU8zvGfnyvbXRoz/IMG_8541.JPG)
The weather is slowly dragging itself toward spring but we have dipped below freezing a few times this week. It may mean that golf season is a ways off but indoor golf is still a great time and one of few sports you can drink beer while playing.
![IMG_8555.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZQ1oJZGD3NhLEZYxHRLce3dcwdS2jwSQvA67TrcAJRgw/IMG_8555.JPG)
I have a backlog of interesting beers to review for #beersaturday because a couple busy weekends have kept me from posting. Fear not as hopefully things will slow down for the next while at least.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# Music
![IMG_8388.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfM6BSgtY9qR6jvsbP7LKbd3xR4bRXRozCLHPJLy9TWsX/IMG_8388.JPG)
I started the month off by heading to the city for a concert. I have seen so many damn concerts over the decades that I have slowed a little as of late. This one brought me out of town because my daughter loves Sloan, I play hockey with one of the guys in the big city, and I had never seen them perform outside of our tournament weekend.
![IMG_8560.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVLcFzeea19ADaYid7xQKQerHPwDtDgpc38fL4irkwUxC/IMG_8560.JPG)
Speaking of hockey tournament music, this past weekend was that weekend. For our act this year, I had to learn some songs one guitar and some on bass as our main bass player couldn't make it this year.
![d1a5ac62-687a-42ec-b6dd-04c16a25818a (2).JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWcW4eXaY9y3XESgMfpgRqCpjbC2r4yD1pSkguuVvL4Ru/d1a5ac62-687a-42ec-b6dd-04c16a25818a%20(2).JPG)
It is quite a trip to head to the city for a couple jams with the guys off in preparation for our show. Time well spent no matter how much gas costs as playing music with the guys is as good as it gets. Funny how many of us have drums sets and amps in our basements. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B02V9qS6SM8 I have to give you my yearly report on our hootenanny show and hockey weekend. Too much of a story for this update but here is a song I came up with to play in the dressing rooms for fun using an image from our show this weekend.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTxLuq7kyd9rMd34typzXZHkbqsukjqdWXvpWfTra7Amb/image.png)
# Spring Rocks!
![IMG_8503.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRgokzJQ9h4ATiXWj3DqDP4kDzUPtG8iFnCiEXDsHUPYM/IMG_8503.JPG)
I will wrap up your Zekely report here before I spill too many spoilers. Thusly, the sun has set on another wild month and I am ready for a little lull before the summer sets in. # Thanks for checking in on all the business, beer and music!
![image (9).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/23zufAZhV9dt6F5XnFS8u5zdRtARKHnwZT4CZECiscnUBWMzc2vsH7vZuFSXcNNuyGDo5.png)

I like it when memorable outings come up during a trip, and I was sure that would happen once I reunited with my friend Noe in Paraguay. We had both had a great experience during our volunteer work in Salta, Argentina, and I was hoping the same would happen while we explored Asunción. Since she had already been in the city for over a month, she moved around the streets comfortably, which was helpful for me to have an almost-local guide and to discover places I wouldn’t have visited on my own 😃.
Me gusta cuando en el viaje surgen paseos memorables y estaba segura de que eso pasaría una vez que me reencontrara con mi amiga Noe en Paraguay. Las dos habíamos tenido una grata experiencia durante nuestro voluntariado en Salta, Argentina, y esperaba que pasara lo mismo mientras visitábamos Asunción. Como ella ya llevaba más de un mes en la ciudad, ya se manejaba cómodamente en las calles, lo que a mí me sirvió para tener una guía casi local, y para descubrir lugares que sola no hubiese visitado 😃.
--- ---
--- --- One of the afternoons I was walking around Asunción, Noe told me about a bar she wanted us to visit. She hadn’t been there before, so she thought it would be a good idea to discover it together. As usual, I don’t really pay much attention to where we’re going—I just trust my guide at the time and start walking. Since Asunción is a big city, I knew we would be walking quite a bit, so I put on comfortable clothes and we headed toward an area called Loma de San Jerónimo.
Una de las tardes que estuve paseando por Asunción, Noe me comentó sobre un bar que quería que visitemos. Ella no lo conocía, así que pensó que sería buena idea descubrirlo juntas. Como siempre, yo nunca me fijo muy bien hacia donde vamos: solo confío en mi guía de turno y empiezo a caminar. Como Asunción es una ciudad grande, supe que caminaríamos bastante, así que me puse ropa cómoda y salimos hacia una zona llamada Loma de San Gerónimo.
---
--- Big cities have their beautiful sides, but also their less touristy areas, and I admit that when I saw we were getting quite far from the center, I got a bit scared. I was even more uneasy when we started looking for the bar in a neighborhood full of small passageways and staircases. Everything looked very picturesque and well-kept, but at the same time it was quiet and almost empty. I’m not very brave when it comes to possible insecurity, but I tried not to think about it and just enjoy the walk while Noe tried to guide us to the bar through that maze.
Las ciudades grandes tienen sus partes lindas pero también tienen sus partes no tan turísticas, y admito que cuando vi que nos estábamos alejando bastante del centro me asusté un poco. Y más aún me asusté cuando empezamos a buscar el bar dentro de un barrio lleno de pequeños pasillos y escaleras. Todo se veía muy pintoresco y bien cuidado, pero a la vez silencioso y casi sin gente. Yo no soy nada valiente frente a la posible inseguridad, pero traté de no pensar en eso y disfrutar el paseo mientras Noe intentaba guiarnos hasta el bar entre todo ese laberinto.
---
---
---
---
--- After walking for quite a while and finally accepting that we had gotten lost, Noe and I found a small store that was open and asked if there really was a bar in that area. It was a relief to know there was and to receive clear directions on how to get there. It turned out the bar was located on the terrace of a house, just a few passageways away from where we were at that moment. We both found it strange what kind of bar it would be in such a hard-to-reach place, but it was a pleasant surprise to discover that it did exist and was even more beautiful than we had imagined.
Después de caminar un buen rato y finalmente aceptar que nos habíamos perdido, Noe y yo encontramos un almacén abierto y preguntamos si efectivamente había un bar en esa zona. Nos alivió saber que si y recibir indicaciones precisas sobre cómo llegar a él. Resultó que el bar se encontraba en la terraza de una casa, a unos cuantos pasillos de donde estábamos en ese momento. A las dos nos resultaba raro el tipo de bar que sería en este lugar tan complicado para llegar, pero fue una buena sorpresa descubrir que efectivamente el lugar existía y era más hermoso de lo que pensábamos.
---
--- Since we had visited this place during siesta time, it wasn’t open when we arrived, but the owner kindly opened the door for us and let us in. We were surprised by the trust he placed in us, because all the drinks at the bar were available and he simply left us there alone to enjoy the space. Everything looked very new and beautiful, as picturesque as the neighborhood below. It would have been great to see it open and at night, but I wasn’t sure if I wanted to walk through those passageways later on.
Como habíamos visitado este lugar en la hora de la siesta, no estaba abierto para cuando llegamos, pero su dueño amablemente nos abrió la puerta y nos dejó pasar. Nos sorprendió la confianza que nos tuvo, porque todas las bebidas del bar estaban a disposición y él simplemente nos dejó ahí solas disfrutando del espacio. Todo se veía muy nuevo y lindo, pintoresco como el barrio más abajo. Hubiese sido genial verlo abierto y de noche, pero no estaba segura de si quería caminar en esos pasillos más tarde.
---
--- Without a doubt, the best part of this bar was the beautiful views of the city. Being a bit elevated already allowed you to see Asunción from above. The afternoon was lovely, and we stayed for quite a while taking photos, as well as charging our phones to continue with the outing. By then, all the adrenaline I had built up on the way there was starting to fade, and I was able to relax after the successful adventure. Deep down, I knew Noe wouldn’t get us into trouble 😂.
Sin dudas, la mejor parte de este bar eran las hermosas vistas de la ciudad. Estar un poco en altura ya te permitía ver Asunción desde lo alto. La tarde estaba hermosa, y nos quedamos un buen rato haciendo una sesión de fotos, además de cargando nuestros celulares para continuar con el paseo. Para entonces, toda la adrenalina que había acumulado en el trayecto de ida ya se estaba disolviendo, y puse relajarme frente al paseo exitoso. En el fondo sabía que Noe no iba a meternos en problemas 😂.
---
--- Visiting this bar, called Guaraní Lounge, was a great memory from my stay in Paraguay. I was glad we found it and that we were able to see a bit of Asunción from above. Even though I knew we wouldn’t be doing any trekking in the city, this trip still involved quite a bit of walking and getting a nice view from up high. That’s what I love about less planned trips—the best stories are created along the way ❤️.
Visitar este bar, llamado Guaraní Lounge, fue un buen recuerdo dentro de mi estadía en Paraguay. Me alegré que lo hayamos encontrado y que hayamos podido ver un poco de Asunción desde arriba. Si bien sabía que en la ciudad no haríamos nada de trekking, este viaje tuvo su cuota de caminar bastante y obtener una buena vista desde la altura. Esto es lo que me gusta de los viajes no tan planeados: las mejores anécdotas se van creando sobre la marcha ❤️.

Dear chessfans,
finally S22 is here, first round will start this Friday, at the usual time (19h GMT)!

The results and stats of the previous season 21 you can look up in [this post](https://peakd.com/hive-157286/@stayoutoftherz/hivechess-season-21-final-results-the-champions-and-the-numbers-and-some-questions), the payouts of S21 (in total **2350** Hive, you can check it [here](https://peakd.com/hive-157286/@stayoutoftherz/hivechess-fun-tournament-this-friday-20h-gmt)), so we can focus straight on what lies ahead!

S22 will go over 10 rounds and unlike in the past there will be 2 completely separate tournaments, the "Masters" for players with a minimum rating of 1800 and the "Challangers" for all other players. The top 3 of the Challengers tournament have the right to play in next season´s Master tournament if there is one (but they don´t need to if they don´t want).

Both tournaments have for now ***restricted entrys by rating***. What does this mean? If you have less than 1800 you cannot play in the Masters, but you can in the Challengers. And vice versa, if you have more than 1800, you can´t play in the Challengers. Of note, if you had 1800 or above *at any point during the last week prior to the tournament date*, you as well can only play in the Masters even if you rating dropped <1800 since then! This rule was setup by Lichess to prevent sandbagging.
If you change your rating over the 10 weeks? You just continue in the other tournament and keep your points. Same if you accidentally played in the Masters, but now are below 1800 again. You take your points from this tournament but stay in the Challengers one. 

Unlike in the past I won´t track the tournament performance this time. It was a lot of work with little benefit. And the percentage of post rewards feeding the prize pool is this season 65% (up from 60%). @badge-646464 will be used to accrue the prizes for S22, so please make this account a small beneficiary on your S22-related posts, to support the season rewards. Such beneficiary posts will be upvoted by me much better, so it may be a win-win.

![Kopia – Whispers.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23xyi6ueGf3YuTPgs57te64jf1bjq5n1ifdeDRyucCfQDSQ6Q2k6xmEKHziyJmKzmj9fy.jpg)


As promised earlier, I invite you to another set of frames from HEIDELBERG. This time it won’t be Heidelberg seen from the riverside, but Heidelberg viewed from above.

>Zgodnie ze swoją wcześniejszą obietnicą zapraszam na kolejną odsłonę kadrów z HEIDELBERGU. Tym razem nie będzie to Heidelberg pokazany znad rzeki, a będzie to Heidelberg widziany z góry.

I started my visit to Heidelberg with the famous path SCHLANGENWEG. It is a very well-known walking path leading up the hills on the other side of the Neckar River, opposite the Old Town.
Translated literally the name means “snake path” and refers to its winding, serpentine route. The path begins near the Old Bridge and leads steeply uphill. If I remember correctly the route is about two kilometers long.
I have to admit that it was quite physically demanding for me. In some places it is really steep and at certain points you have to climb up stone steps.

>Swoją wizytę w Heidelbergu rozpoczęłam od słynnej ścieżki "SCHLANGENWEG". Jest to bardzo znana ścieżka spacerowa prowadząca na wzgórza po drugiej stronie rzeki Neckar, naprzeciwko Starego Miasta. Tłumacząc dosłownie nazwa oznacza "wężową ścieżkę" i odnosi się oczywiście do jej serpentyn i krętych ścieżek. Ścieżka ta zaczyna się w pobliżu Starego Mostu, prowadzi stromo pod górę. O ile dobrze pamiętam, trasa wynosi około dwóch kilometrów. Muszę przyznać, że była to trasa dla mnie bardzo wymagająca fizycznie. Miejscami jest tam naprawdę stromo, gdzieniegdzie na górę prowadzą nas kamienne schody.



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23xedt74gBj9xDsAKN5UHtDXtpDbL5i9UHFW7ibRYSA5gZV3Q2gFsoaHbTKWdd3sZtCE1.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23uFTh84RQvqeNWsP2Fhobw6bT69UvzGZg5TmMbQhzy1Ysd3jCj1s7gxuCJw9aLmpnxku.png)


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23wgHutb4wRom93vMsZbWZfNjm4JAtP7SoHXTMt5nqnjKj3Ao9cUsUueWe758nwt4yBqX.png)

Without a doubt the biggest advantage of this walk was the picturesque views. Almost the entire time while climbing up the hill, it was possible to admire the panorama of Heidelberg, the Neckar River and the Old Town.

If you want to see the city from above, with its contrasting rooftops, this is definitely one of the best places in the city.

>Niewątpliwie największą zaletą tego spaceru były malownicze widoki. Praktycznie przez cały czas wspinając się na to wzgórze, można było podziwiać panoramę Heidelbergu, rzekę Neckar oraz stare miasto.
>
>Jeśli chcemy zobaczyć miasto z góry, kontrastowe dachy, to będzie to niewątpliwie jedno z lepszych miejsc w mieście.


![20250726_114753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/EoAYEVTRqve1k4dAf38mVZiPwk6UayviR5ZzKSj6fJbybvDts6km7vgxbu4utwDgmyk.jpg)

![20250726_112647.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/Eou6j4c8tdQuNbipYMM6ED8TRqjyLK4rAPcmz2TZJ2B6Gqe5G1NNSQ4keafmwotuBwq.jpg)

![20250726_130728.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/Eq7LSANesZ4J6EhPcW7iDJD54m1nuetVcMkg4gXXMhY16U4dh1H6N438hN3uuroobMy.jpg)

The most iconic landmark of Heidelberg is, of course, its beautiful castle, also located on a hill. While walking along the Schlangenweg, you can admire the castle from a distance, as it blends perfectly into the surrounding hills.
However I won’t go into detail about the castle today, as it is interesting enough to deserve a separate post.

>Największą wizytówką miasta Heidelberg jest oczywiście jego przepiękny zamek, zlokalizowany również na wzgórzu. Spacerując Schlangenweg możemy również podziwiać zamek z daleka, który pięknie komponuje się ze wzgórzami. Nie będę jednak dzisiaj się rozpisywała na temat tego zamku, gdyż jest on na tyle interesujący, że zasługuje na osobny post.


![20250726_114732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tbiNH2RDswojtQG6rWBhx3SLjet3fKbTKRSerbdPVjhTx59juARyBWzSUK2QmZxv295.jpg)

For the way back I chose a different walking path, which was definitely less demanding. I slightly regretted not doing it the other way around. It would have been much easier to go uphill on an asphalt road and come back via the Schlangenweg.
But as we say in Poland : "a person becomes wise after the damage is done" 😁

>Na drogę powrotną wybrałam inną ścieżkę spacerową, która była zdecydowanie mniej wymagająca. Trochę żałowałam, że nie zrobiłam tego odwrotnie. O wiele łatwiej byłoby wspinać się na górę drogą asfaltową, a wracać Schlangenweg. No ale jest takie przysłowie w Polsce : "Polak mądry po szkodzie" 😁


![20250726_113303.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tSL9RaRbuZS7QEREYAsiSrkosdzfzBk8oTwjFM6pJKSKcn8YoQNd6azcBBwfprH6MVK.jpg)

---
*The photo above is my entry for #aroundtheworld contest*

---

![20250726_130745.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23u5vxcXfXTBLMZbRaWCLG2tgL3phaihxUL2T6NEonjWobE1nvXtVPaUoUAgzQSbXcPDF.jpg)

![20250726_114021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tvW8xFHtEPQZ3Vha23EyCN4ysBNRQ5cR98PDLiYan1uyA7ce7CBUbJipCPEkSr8Uokf.jpg)

After this exhausting walk I headed towards the castle. As I mentioned earlier, photos of the castle will appear on my profile another day. The castle is very large and very interesting, so I took a lot of photos.

Today, however, I would like to share with you the view I found on the hill where the castle is located. It is another place in Heidelberg where you can admire the view of the Old Town, directly from above.

From this point you could clearly see the dense urban layout of Heidelberg. What also caught my attention were the red rooftops. Almost all the buildings were in the same color, which created a very pleasing composition.

>Po tym wyczerpującym spacerze udałam się w stronę zamku. Jak już wcześniej wspomniałam zdjęcia zamku pojawią się innego dnia na moim profilu. Zamek jest bardzo duży i bardzo ciekawy. Zrobiłam bardzo dużo zdjęć, a dzisiaj chciałabym podzielić się z wami widokiem, który zastałam na wzgórzu, na którym jest zlokalizowany zamek. 
>
>Jest to kolejne miejsce w Heidelbergu, w którym można podziwiać widok bezpośredio na Stare Miasto. Z góry doskonale było widać zwartą zabudowę miasta Heidelbergu. Moją uwagę również zwróciły czerwone dachy. Praktycznie wszystkie budynki były w tym samym kolorze, co świetnie się to komponowało.


![20250726_130810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23vhsGMLuXSbq7WVCu2iXXTCGnvdCVSh7wRMjKiftmgQG8RWWHK9WVCaXki7Tmj1ABT5A.jpg)

In the panorama of Heidelberg one building stood out in particular — the CHURCH OF THE HOLY SPIRIT. It is one of the most important and characteristic buildings in Heidelberg. It is located in the very heart of the Old Town, right by the market square and is the largest church in the city. It was built mainly in the Gothic style between the 14th and 16th centuries.

>W panoramie Heidelbergu szczególnie wyróżniał się jeden budynek, a mianowicie KOŚCIÓŁ DUCHA ŚWIĘTEGO. Jest to jeden z najważniejszych i najbardziej charakterystycznych budynków w Heidelbergu. Znajduje się w samym sercu Starego Miasta, tuż przy rynku i jest największym kościołem w mieście. Został zbudowany głównie w stylu gotyckim między XIV a XVI wiekiem.


![20250726_131021.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23tvVvYsgsXAB952ZUAEZuPwcfGvYRF8bRx79Q3gFvh5HP5hsQxVzXHEEwrRMs7p2KSYR.jpg)

![20250726_130957.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23y8mWM7UvbtBG8xePmJMjuc3Ye2kXed4aUEGk8d3mYJ2LBZbTGtnE64Z2b3WYoLYNW18.jpg)


It was another successful weekend on the road. I’m already looking forward to more weekends like this.🤗

🇬🇧 Kazbegi Walk Promenade à Kazbegi Paseo por Kazbegi Paseo por Kazbegi 🇫🇷 🇪🇸

* * * * *
* * * * *
🇬🇧 This Wednesday’s walk starts from the village of Kazbegi. At the gateway to the Greater Caucasus, north of Tbilisi, the village of Stepantsminda, better known by its former name Kazbegi, embodies one of the most beautiful postcard scenes in Georgia. Here, the Georgian Military Road winds between deep valleys and steep peaks, offering panoramas that seem unreal as you climb higher into the mountains. Kazbegi is not just a stopover, it is a destination in its own right, a place where the pace slows down and where you take the time to contemplate a nature that remains largely untouched. The village itself, modest and surrounded by hills, serves as a starting point for many hikes, attracting travellers and lovers of wide open spaces. Despite its tourist development, Kazbegi retains an authentic, almost timeless atmosphere, where local traditions coexist with the warm hospitality of its inhabitants. There is a sense of raw simplicity here, far from big cities, where every sunrise and sunset reshapes the landscape with an almost dramatic intensity. 🇫🇷 La promenade de ce mercredi part du village de Kazbegi. Aux portes du Grand Caucase, au nord de Tbilissi, le village de Stepantsminda, plus connu sous son ancien nom de Kazbegi, incarne l’une des plus belles cartes postales de Géorgie. Ici, la route militaire géorgienne serpente entre vallées profondes et sommets abrupts, offrant des panoramas qui semblent irréels à mesure que l’on s’élève vers les montagnes. Kazbegi n’est pas seulement une étape, c’est une destination à part entière, un lieu où le rythme ralentit et où l’on prend le temps de contempler une nature encore largement préservée. Le village lui-même, modeste et entouré de collines, sert de point de départ à de nombreuses randonnées, attirant voyageurs et amoureux de grands espaces. Malgré son développement touristique, Kazbegi conserve une atmosphère authentique, presque intemporelle, où les traditions locales cohabitent avec l’accueil chaleureux des habitants. On y ressent une forme de simplicité brute, loin des grandes villes, où chaque lever et coucher de soleil redessine les reliefs avec une intensité presque dramatique. 🇪🇸 El paseo de este miércoles comienza en el pueblo de Kazbegi. A las puertas del Gran Cáucaso, al norte de Tiflis, el pueblo de Stepantsminda, más conocido por su antiguo nombre Kazbegi, encarna una de las postales más bellas de Georgia. Aquí, la carretera militar georgiana serpentea entre valles profundos y cumbres abruptas, ofreciendo panoramas que parecen irreales a medida que se asciende hacia las montañas. Kazbegi no es solo una etapa, es un destino en sí mismo, un lugar donde el ritmo se ralentiza y donde se toma el tiempo de contemplar una naturaleza que sigue siendo en gran parte intacta. El propio pueblo, modesto y rodeado de colinas, sirve como punto de partida para numerosas rutas de senderismo, atrayendo a viajeros y amantes de los grandes espacios. A pesar de su desarrollo turístico, Kazbegi conserva una atmósfera auténtica, casi atemporal, donde las tradiciones locales conviven con la cálida hospitalidad de sus habitantes. Se percibe una forma de simplicidad pura, lejos de las grandes ciudades, donde cada amanecer y atardecer redibuja el paisaje con una intensidad casi dramática.
* * * * *
🇬🇧 Dominating the region with all its power, Mount Kazbek stands as a majestic and unmissable presence. Rising to over 5,000 metres, this dormant volcano is one of the highest peaks in the Caucasus and a true natural icon of the country. Often wrapped in clouds, it occasionally reveals itself in all its splendour, exposing its snow-covered slopes and glaciers that seem suspended above the void. The mountain is steeped in myths and legends, notably that of Prometheus, who is said to have been chained to its slopes for giving fire to mankind. Whether you are an experienced mountaineer or a simple hiker, the presence of Kazbek fascinates and impresses. It attracts those seeking a challenge, but also those who simply come to admire its imposing silhouette from the valley. Its changing character, sometimes threatening, sometimes soothing, gives the landscape an almost spiritual dimension, reinforcing the feeling of standing before untamed nature. 🇫🇷 Dominant la région de toute sa puissance, le mont Kazbek s’impose comme une présence majestueuse et incontournable. Culminant à plus de 5000 mètres, ce volcan endormi est l’un des plus hauts sommets du Caucase et une véritable icône naturelle du pays. Souvent enveloppé de nuages, il se dévoile par moments dans toute sa splendeur, laissant apparaître ses pentes enneigées et ses glaciers qui semblent suspendus au-dessus du vide. La montagne est chargée de mythes et de légendes, notamment celle de Prométhée, qui aurait été enchaîné sur ses flancs pour avoir offert le feu aux hommes. Que l’on soit alpiniste expérimenté ou simple randonneur, la présence du Kazbek fascine et impressionne. Il attire ceux qui cherchent le défi, mais aussi ceux qui viennent simplement admirer sa silhouette imposante depuis la vallée. Son caractère changeant, tantôt menaçant, tantôt apaisant, donne au paysage une dimension presque spirituelle, renforçant le sentiment d’être face à une nature indomptable. 🇪🇸 Dominando la región con toda su fuerza, el monte Kazbek se impone como una presencia majestuosa e imprescindible. Con más de 5.000 metros de altura, este volcán dormido es una de las cumbres más altas del Cáucaso y un verdadero icono natural del país. A menudo envuelto en nubes, se revela por momentos en todo su esplendor, mostrando sus laderas nevadas y sus glaciares que parecen suspendidos sobre el vacío. La montaña está cargada de mitos y leyendas, especialmente la de Prometeo, que habría sido encadenado en sus laderas por haber dado el fuego a los hombres. Tanto si se es alpinista experimentado como simple senderista, la presencia del Kazbek fascina e impresiona. Atrae a quienes buscan el desafío, pero también a quienes simplemente vienen a admirar su imponente silueta desde el valle. Su carácter cambiante, a veces amenazante, a veces apacible, otorga al paisaje una dimensión casi espiritual, reforzando la sensación de estar frente a una naturaleza indomable.
* * * * *
🇬🇧 Overlooking the village and facing Mount Kazbek, the Gergeti Trinity Church is undoubtedly one of the most powerful symbols of Georgia. Perched at over 2,100 metres above sea level, it seems to defy the laws of balance, standing alone on its promontory, surrounded by vast mountain landscapes. Built in the 14th century, this Orthodox church is both a place of worship and an iconic visual landmark, attracting visitors, photographers and pilgrims from around the world. The ascent to reach it, whether on foot or by vehicle, is an integral part of the experience, each turn revealing a new perspective over the valley and the surrounding peaks. Once at the top, the silence, the wind and the immensity of the landscape create a unique, almost unreal atmosphere. One then understands why this place is so deeply rooted in the Georgian collective imagination. Between sky and earth, the Gergeti Church embodies the meeting point of spirituality, history and grandiose nature, offering a suspended moment that few places in the world can match. 🇫🇷 Surplombant le village et faisant face au mont Kazbek, l’église de la Trinité de Gergeti est sans doute l’un des symboles les plus puissants de la Géorgie. Perchée à plus de 2100 mètres d’altitude, elle semble défier les lois de l’équilibre, posée seule sur son promontoire, entourée de vastes étendues montagneuses. Construite au XIVe siècle, cette église orthodoxe est à la fois un lieu de culte et un repère visuel emblématique, attirant visiteurs, photographes et pèlerins du monde entier. L’ascension pour y accéder, que ce soit à pied ou en véhicule, fait partie intégrante de l’expérience, chaque virage révélant une nouvelle perspective sur la vallée et les sommets environnants. Une fois en haut, le silence, le vent et l’immensité du paysage créent une atmosphère unique, presque irréelle. Construida en el siglo XIV, esta iglesia ortodoxa es a la vez un lugar de culto y un referente visual emblemático, atrayendo a visitantes, fotógrafos y peregrinos de todo el mundo. La subida para llegar hasta ella, ya sea a pie o en vehículo, forma parte integral de la experiencia, cada curva revelando una nueva perspectiva del valle y de las cumbres circundantes. Entonces se entiende por qué este lugar está tan profundamente arraigado en el imaginario colectivo georgiano. Entre el cielo y la tierra, la iglesia de Gergeti encarna por sí sola el encuentro entre espiritualidad, historia y naturaleza grandiosa, ofreciendo un momento suspendido que pocos lugares en el mundo pueden igualar.

Last week I made the mistake of starting to watch a series without checking it out thoroughly in advance. Not necessarily a bad thing and only becomes a problem if you bump into something you don't like and this was the case with the series. It was the [Midnight Mass](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt10574558/) an American series, categorized as drama, fantasy, horror, mystery. Without wanting to look so full of myself, I think I deserve a medal as despite hating horror, I watched the mini-series till the end. Unfortunately (for them, not for me) it could not make me like horror and can't say it was good, but there was a detail in the series that made me think of a different life I am living now. ![olivier-collet-ZU62GJP-XC4-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23y8qerqUvFkEM8RXYGm9j5mB1VwT9zN3Q9vdGTYsnEWD58SLeuTQ2nauZfnSCho5bjx8.jpg) Photo by Olivier Collet on Unsplash As the description on IMBD says, the story is about an isolated island community. When it says isolated island community, they mean a handful of people, less than 100 and it is clearly stated in the series as well so I was thinking what it would mean, or feel like, to live in such a small community. The current city I am residing in has around 150k inhabitants, so I can't really say it's big and chances to bump into someone you know every single day is high, no matter where you go, what part of the city you visit. Still, you can close your door at home and have your private life as you wish, which is a huge advantage if you care about privacy. There's no dropping by unannounced, just to see what you're doing as these days visits must be agreed on. To small community members this may seem strange, but we all have our lives, routines and schedule and no one wants unexpected guests. ![nick-fewings-Bd1MhsLxeRI-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23tveNjdk7Yr3Mk3obHaHf3wqfNP7bJtCZtedgBzVYcabXE4V9DFGgNRK1yQu2VtgkdH2.jpg) Photo by Nick Fewings on Unsplash When you live in a small place, where everyone knows everyone, your privacy goes out of the window the minute you move there. Wherever you go, whatever you do, everyone is going to find out about it rather sooner, than later. Some movies tend to present this specific case as living in a big, happy family, but we all know that could not be further from the truth. I am always saying that those who don't have a private life, are living other people's life, meaning they gossip, interfere with other people's business, which is why sooner or later someone is going to make you do things you don't want, and stop you from doing things you want, as they think that's the custom or everyone does that. This is how slowly you lose your own way of life and live the life others want you to. ![felix-mittermeier-JYx2nrMrGZo-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/EowFcyGE2oiAvD6tnwTDLaJxo7weg4d6YaEfv9XPcNhNWj2kHeG4eeT4nSWXCkQkgkt.jpg) Photo by Felix Mittermeier on Unsplash It's quite difficult to live in a small community with the mindset you have after living in a city and most likely I could not get used to it. When I'm visiting my dad, sometimes it happens to meet locals (the handful I know there) and I'm happily chatting with them, but at some point you need to limit what you share with them, if you don't want to make the next hour news in the village, or end up in the *bush radio*, as gossip is called there. It depends how you look at it, but for me, most likely it would feel like a prison you can't escape, unless you move or go away. Small communities, with all those secrets. My grandmother was an example in this regard, she was happy to learn every gossip in the village, from those who came to visit, but the biggest joy for her was the part when she distorted the gossips the way she wanted and passed them on to others. Needless to say, her credibility decreased in my eyes as soon as I old enough to be able to understand what this means. ![thierry-lemaitre-Yra5bMGqn20-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/EpLh1tKQ9Xk1dvpTPqLNPfnoYpBtVaULMbBLEhvqCB2nAfJkZvrReULoNkeMfuKepjh.jpg) Photo by Thierry Lemaitre on Unsplash We have users from all around the world on Hive, people from cities with several millions of inhabitants, as well as villagers, who have never left their small village, so most likely opinions are divided on the topic, but I'd be happy to read about your experience and opinion on the matter.

今天儿子学校英语听力口语模拟考试，让我不由得想起3月30日的理化实验考试——也是一次非常重要的考试，成绩计入中考分数呢。


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcARpLtZAf2LdEyWbSvqNnzPv2L8bzzdN4JnPEZK8CvUK/image.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

回想起我们读书的日子，实验还真不是个容易的项目，每步操作、每个细节都要考虑和处理周到，否则老师肯定要给扣一点点分的。

比如化学课加热高锰酸钾制氧气，试管口略微向下倾斜就是很有说道的。你若是操作时试管口倾斜向上，又或者水平放置，就有可能导致“惨烈”的后果，试管炸裂。

还有物理的电学实验课，涉及到使用滑动变阻器的时候，滑变最开始的时候一定要放到最大阻值处，否则就可能出现电路中电流过大烧毁器件或者电流表的惨剧。

话说从小到大，我也算是实践小能手了，初高中的物理化学实验上从未翻过车，但大学一次电学实验，学习集成运算放大器（Integrated Operational Amplifier）时，我忘记调整电源电压，直接把集放干冒烟了。还好我反应比较快，直接把集放甩地上，才没被老师抓现行。


![e0ab2afa022593a1632f2afaba9fb445.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYW2BwYeUqjEYqanZkpAM6Ae3H9wLsMttbydHNYhUNa7v/e0ab2afa022593a1632f2afaba9fb445.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

所以儿子理化考试之前，我很是担忧，万一他那个细节没考虑到、没处理好，被扣分了可咋办？

媳妇说我完全就是多想，以为其它区域先进行的理化考试，据那些家长反馈，几乎每班都是全员满分。

当然也有例外的，据说有个学校的某个学生到了实验室就一动不动，老师一直督促他动一下手，说但凡动一下手，就给满分，但是那学生就不动，老师也是没辙了，没给满分。

话虽如此，但是谁知道到我们区会不会严格呀？或者会不会遇到较真的老师？我准备在考前头一天帮儿子复习一下实验相关内容，不过他根本就不在意，说自己胸有成竹。哎，那就不管了，顺其自然吧。

儿子考试当天，我那个担心劲就甭提了，盼呀盼呀总算盼到了放学。接到儿子后，问理化试验考得怎么样，儿子说当然都是满分了。

问同学们考得都咋样，他说全班同学都满分。我又问那就没有说不会做实验的嘛？他说有呀，但是监考老师（也都是外校老师）会帮忙做。我😵，还有这种操作。

他还给我讲，监考老师甚至把评分单直接给同学们，让他们愿意填多少分就填多少分。我晕，我麻木了。

我又问儿子做的两个实验，他说化学实验是配置一定百分比的氯化钠溶液，说实验器材竟然没有玻璃棒，他告诉监考老师缺玻璃棒，监考老师说玻璃棒丢了，你晃晃就可以啦。物理实验是测电阻两端电压、电流的关系，说实验器材也都缺胳膊少腿的。


![a9492eb8126d0b51a6e72955892d4cd7.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWSZ7NqqNFi25KFjYoHr36kAMQ4BaQCEUDMQwsjiKd8iq/a9492eb8126d0b51a6e72955892d4cd7.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

哎，也不知道整个走形式的理化实验考试，是出于什么考虑呢？培养学生们的动手能力？但是这样真的能培养的出来嘛？一声叹息！

不过理化实验都满分，还是好事一桩，至少我不用在这个事情上瞎操心了（他们娘俩都没担心过）
